Arrival: 09/20/2024 04:14 (POV, accompanied by spouse)
Triage: 04:17 by RN T. Mendez. ESI Level 2.

TRIAGE NOTE (RN Mendez):
"Pt presents c/o severe HA × 6h, 'worst headache of my life.' Reports neck stiffness, light sensitivity, fever to 102 at home. Pt appears acutely ill. VSS: HR 124, BP 142/88, T 102.4 oral, RR 22, SpO2 95% RA. Concern for meningitis — flagged to ED MD."

MD NOTE (Holbrook, 05:48):
HPI: 56 y.o. male with 6-hour history of severe HA, fever, neck stiffness, photophobia. No recent travel, no sick contacts, no rash. Vaccinations UTD per pt. No prior similar episodes.

PE: Alert, A&Ox3 but ill-appearing. Neck supple to passive flexion, mild discomfort. Kernig negative, Brudzinski negative. No focal neuro deficits. No rash. Chest clear. Abd soft.

ASSESSMENT: Severe headache, fever — DDx includes viral syndrome, migraine, less likely meningitis (no overt nuchal rigidity, Kernig/Brudzinski negative).
PLAN: CT head w/o contrast, CBC, BMP, blood cultures × 2, IV NS, acetaminophen 1g.

[NO LP ORDERED. NO EMPIRIC ANTIBIOTICS ORDERED.]

CT HEAD RESULT (08:14): Negative for mass effect, hemorrhage, hydrocephalus.

MD NOTE (Holbrook, 08:22):
CT negative. Most likely viral syndrome vs. atypical migraine. Will admit to medicine for symptomatic management and serial neuro checks. Hospitalist Petrov contacted.

HOSPITALIST ACCEPT NOTE (Petrov, 09:12):
Accept for admission. Continue supportive care. Repeat exam on the floor. Plan LP if no improvement by AM rounds.

[Patient transferred to floor at 11:40.]

NURSING NOTE (Floor RN Nguyen, 14:30): "Pt c/o worsening HA, now febrile to 103.1. Appears more lethargic. Called to MD."

MD NOTE (Petrov, 15:48): "Pt clinically worse since admit. Initiating empiric abx (ceftriaxone 2g IV + vanc 1g IV). LP to be performed."

FIRST DOSE ANTIBIOTICS ADMINISTERED: 17:15, 09/20/2024.
LP PERFORMED: 22:08, 09/20/2024.
